claim: On the Ti2-E the light path has four addresses: 1 is the eyepiece observation port; 2 the right side port; 3, with the optical-path split prism, sends 80 per cent to the left side port and 20 per cent to the eyepieces, or is the bottom port on the Ti2-E/B; and 4 is the left side port. So two addresses can put light into the eyepieces. The position the path takes at start-up is a Ti2 Control setting.
validity_conditions: Read from Nikon Ti2 Control Ver2.90 for Windows, English manual M706 E15 (sha256 5e43517c...): printed page 67 (PDF page 75), printed page 75 (PDF page 83). E3 vendor_spec: the manufacturer's statement, not an observation on this bench. This manual is for the Ti2 Control software; the archive holds no Ti2-E hardware manual. How these addresses map onto Micro-Manager's LightPath state numbers is not stated in the manual; on 2026-09-24 state 3 read back with the label '4-L100' (stand_state_read_20260924_20x_in_place), which fits address = state + 1 and does not establish it. Whether this stand has the split prism is not recorded here. KNOWLEDGE, NOT POLICY: this is what the manufacturer says. What any session may do, and every limit anyone here acts on, is the person's, written into the envelope after confirming it on the instrument.
